what: generate-root stopped with 'manual changes in generated files' on .gitignore after the generated project was copied into the existing repo.
why: The builder copied the generator output over the repo's tracked .gitignore, so the generator saw a hand edit. The catalog does not say how to adopt generated files into a repo that already has its own .gitignore.
workaround: Restored the generated .gitignore, added .pi/dashboard/kb/ to .git/info/exclude, reran generate-root (exit 0).

what: Guessed the ESM type name Namespace in a query and got an error.
why: Type name was not checked against the metamodel before the query. Minor.
workaround: Queried the real types (Model, Package, StringType, NumericType) instead.

what: ActorType create warned that realm does not apply, because the actor was effectively anonymous.
why: The builder left anonymous unset while setting a realm. The accesspoint doc says realm applies only when the actor is not anonymous.
workaround: Second update set realm, managed=false and kind on webshop::Shop; the warning went away.

what: The builder improvised the first-user fix before searching the kb. Its final report said the catalog had no recipe, then the kb search found the JIT provisioning doc and the platform behaviour section.
why: The kb-first habit was not applied at the start. The catalog did cover the row side (AuthenticationInterceptor JIT), though not the Keycloak user side.
workaround: Recorded as GAPS 15a after the user asked for kb-first on problems.

what: Said the app was slow to respond (15 to 40 s per click). The orchestrator later showed the server answers in milliseconds.
why: Wrong diagnosis from unreliable browser clicks; no curl timing was done to check.
workaround: Kept the fixed waits.

what: Shell commands used on macOS: GNU 'timeout' is not installed, and a find / scan timed out after 60 s.
why: Builder assumed a Linux shell and ran a whole-disk find.
workaround: Dropped timeout and ran Maven directly.

what: Clicked Back on a view page opened directly by URL. Back did nothing, because the breadcrumb stack was empty.
why: Breadcrumb navigation records only in-app navigation. The builder expected browser history.
workaround: Re-ran the path list to view, then Back, which worked.

what: Tried create -t MenuItemAccess, which the CLI rejects because MenuItemAccess is created automatically for an actor's access.
why: Builder tried the create command on an auto-generated element.
workaround: Used create -t Access on the actor and let the CLI create the menu access.

what: Builder assumed ./judo.sh generate would regenerate the frontend table component after reverting the S04 patch. It did not; the frontend build (judo.sh build -f -i) was needed.
why: Builder assumed the generate step covers frontend files; it only writes the scaffolds and model-derived sources.
workaround: Ran ./judo.sh build -f -i, after which the table component was regenerated.

what: Builder used fixed waits (wait 4000, 5000, 6000 ms) while checking in the browser, against the round rule to wait for an element or URL.
why: Builder did not follow the round's check rule.

what: Login attempts failed because the builder typed the password into the wrong field and used the wrong input commands (quoted text, keyboard inserttext mixed with type). The builder then had to retype the password.
why: Builder's own typing mix-up in the browser, not a server fault.
workaround: Cleared the fields and retyped both with the type command, then signed in.

what: Builder used eval to read document.activeElement while checking focus, which is outside the check rules. It said so in its notes.
why: Builder wanted to confirm focus state; the round rules ban eval for clicks and deep links, and this was a read.

what: Round 1 screenshots at 375, 768 and 1440 px all failed because checks/S04 did not exist. The builder then deleted the screenshots and wrote a README saying the round's checks were not completed.
why: Builder did not create the output folders before taking screenshots.
workaround: Created checks/S04 and checks/S09, then removed the partial screenshots and recorded the incomplete check in README.md.

what: Builder's macOS shell mistakes: the GNU timeout wrapper is not installed (timeout: command not found), a sed call on generator-parameter.properties used the wrong -i form, and it appended then removed a property line; the property ended up true.
why: Builder's own shell editing mistake; the property is a one-line change.
workaround: Re-ran sed with the correct form; grep confirmed generateE2eModule=true.

what: Edit-form fill on the price input failed with 'element is not editable'. The cause was the builder's own PriceField, which set readOnly = !editMode while the view page starts with editMode false. The builder removed that condition and rebuilt.
why: Builder's component logic: read-only was tied to the page edit flag, which is false until the first change.
workaround: PriceField readOnly now only depends on __updateable; rebuilt and reran.

what: Round 2 report says there were several test runs and fixes in the end phase, although the round rule was to run the tests once at the end.
why: Builder ran the suite repeatedly to find selector and editability failures.

what: Orchestrator found the product descriptions are placeholder text 'a / b'. Real descriptions of 2 to 3 lines are required for the 3 products, entered through the UI in a test, not through SQL.
why: Builder seeded minimal test data for the description field.
workaround: Round 3 task: restore real descriptions through the UI.

what: Builder removed .git/index.lock by hand after a git add failed, after checking pgrep. A lock file can belong to a running git process.
why: Builder's shortcut to finish the commit; the lock message said to make sure no git process ran.
workaround: Commit succeeded as b69df6a.

what: Round 3 test run failed 10 tests with ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED because Docker was not running. judo.sh start printed 'Cannot connect to the Docker daemon' and the builder's wait loop ended before the app came up, so the tests ran against a dead server.
why: Docker Desktop was stopped; the builder did not check the Docker daemon before starting the stack.
workaround: Started Docker, stopped and restarted the stack, waited for HTTP 200, then reran the tests.

what: TypeScript build error in the new CatalogHome.tsx: a helper typed (text?: string) was called with a string or null value, failing TS2345 and the build once.
why: Builder's own type annotation did not allow null from the generated product description.
workaround: Changed the helper parameter to string | null; the next build passed.

what: Builder ran many repeated source searches (ls/grep/sed on catalog and CLI output) without calling kb_search; the guard warned seven times.
why: Builder defaulted to reading CLI output and source instead of kb-first discipline required by the standing rules.
workaround: Builder continued; later kb_search calls were made.

what: update --feature name failed on CategoryInfo and ProductInfo: name is not a placeable feature on the table or view element because the feature is on the nested relation.
why: Builder targeted the wrong element; the feature belongs to the nested category or products relation.
workaround: Targeted the nested element instead (CategoryInfo_View_Edit products column).

what: Builder ran a bare tsc command that is not the project compiler; the tool printed a wrong-command banner.
why: Builder ran a command outside the project toolchain.
workaround: Builder moved on to the build script.

what: Seed test looked for catalog-grid and then for a generic no-rows text; both locators were guessed, and the test failed on each before it matched the real markup.
why: The builder guessed selectors instead of reading the e2e locator conventions.
workaround: Replaced locators with or() alternatives and the table row locator.

what: Seed helper passed the dialog as the locator for the Unit and Category pickers; their option popups render outside the dialog, so the option click timed out, and the relation waited on a range response that never came.
why: The popup rendered outside the dialog scope; the builder scoped the locator to the dialog.
workaround: Opened the combobox in the dialog and clicked the option from the page scope; used pressSequentially for the category.

what: Builder built the category view with a Products button that opens a list instead of an embedded table on the view, which FUNCTIONS.md asks for.
why: Builder chose a button representation and did not follow the table-on-view pattern from the catalog.
workaround: Round 7 correction: switched to an inline table on the view (see c03-40).

what: graphql and CLI queries used Claim name or a claim fqn that does not exist (Customer username USERNAME, Claim name field); the query or update failed.
why: Builder assumed the Claim type has a name field; the schema does not expose it under that name.
workaround: Queried Claim fqn only.

what: Renaming the username member to email with a new type left the mapped member on the actor info transfer object with the old type; validate warned the data type must match its binding.
why: A rename plus type change must be applied to the mapped member too; the builder changed only the entity side first.
workaround: Renamed the mapped member in the same script step.

what: Several Round 7 steps read generated Java and TypeScript (sdk, internal, frontend services, ImageDisplay) with grep and python without a prior kb_search; the standing rule says the kb comes first and the gap must be logged.
why: Builder went to generated code directly to learn the DAO, query and image APIs and did not log a kb miss in GAPS.md.
workaround: Used the generated API it found; no GAPS entry was made for the lookup at that point.

what: Builder added src/custom/application-customizer.tsx to .generator-ignore in the admin and customer frontend modules, against the standing rule that .generator-ignore entries are never added.
why: The only documented registration point is a generated file; the R1-3 exception was approved only for the shop module, and the builder applied it to two new modules.
workaround: Left the entries in place; not reverted in this chunk.

what: The customer API returned stock, active and variants on the product list and details (data leak), because the customer used the admin-facing product transfer object.
why: Own design mistake from earlier rounds: the customer product access pointed at the mapped ProductInfo, which carries admin-only fields.
workaround: New mapped transfer object ShopProductInfo without stock, active and variants; Customer.products points at it; ProductInfo stays admin only; test watches server answers for a browsing customer.

what: The builder did not consult the kb before source searches: about 20 kb guard warnings ('repeated source searching, still no kb consult'); the orchestrator later counted kb 6 of 161 calls.
why: Builder habit: catalog and generated code were read with ctx_execute and grep instead of kb_search and kb_get first.

what: A reload added to the screenshot helper (to lay out the drawer) closed open dialogs, so six admin tests failed until the reload was removed.
why: Own test-helper mistake made while fixing R8-1.
workaround: Removed the reload calls from the helpers; admin suite then passed 30 of 30.

what: Builder read or grepped generated code (SDK, frontend services, customization files) many times after the kb had no answer or was skipped; the kb guard warned about several consecutive source searches roughly fifteen times in the round.
why: kb-first rule not applied consistently; the kb share was low (orchestrator: 19 of 168 calls).
workaround: Recovered by reading the kb after each warning; catalog answers were found for most later lookups.

what: A model edit script was run a second time without discard, so every element was created twice; validate reported 38, then 50 errors. discard refused without --force.
why: Script was not idempotent and the builder did not check unsaved CLI state before re-running it.
workaround: discard --force, then one clean run of the script.

what: Repeated shell slips: head -0 errors, a log file never written because of a brace redirect (ENOENT twice), a script line that referenced an element created later, and a broad find over the home folder that timed out after 60 seconds.
why: Hand-written shell scripts and broad searches.
workaround: Re-ran with correct paths and order.

what: Order history on the admin view was not sorted by time (Shipped to Delivered listed before Order placed).
why: The history column had no default sort; the builder did not set one in R9.
workaround: Set sort=ASC on the history column happenedAt (DataColumn sort); test checks the four rows in time order.

what: Invoice and coupon actions were placed directly into the view again (OperationForm outside an ActionGroup), giving ActionContainerSameWithActionDefinition and NamedElementHaveToBeInApplication errors.
why: Builder repeated the R8-7 mistake; the lesson was not applied.
workaround: Deleted the actions, moved them into an ActionGroup with relocate, validate passed.

what: F29 test failed with ReferenceError: reactivate is not defined after a cleanup block was pasted into the wrong test.
why: Test edit slip; three tests failed in the full customer run.
workaround: Moved the cleanup block; level4 re-run alone passed 7 of 7.

what: Full customer Playwright suite was not run again after the final test fix; the report says so. The standing rule asks for the whole suite once at the end.
why: Last fix was verified only by re-running level4 alone.
workaround: None in the round.

what: kb-first rule slipped again: source greps and generated-code reads between kb calls; the kb guard warned at least six times; orchestrator counted 8 of 116 kb calls.
why: Builder reached for grep and generated code before the kb.
workaround: kb consulted after each warning; several answers found.

what: A derived flag written as a JQL negation on a boolean (filter with !n.read) failed to parse; the builder then used n.read == false.
why: Builder used a negation form without checking the kb first; the catalog documents the 'not' keyword in model-development.md.
workaround: Rewrote the expression as n.read == false.

what: validate reported 46 'Named element X is not unique in its container' errors after the model edit script ran twice on top of partly applied changes; discard refused without --force and the validate output dumped the EVL path instead of the failing element.
why: Non-idempotent create script re-run after a failed run without discarding; CLI discard requires --force and the error text is not actionable.
workaround: discard --force, then re-ran the script from a clean model.

what: CSV import test used SKUs like IMP-A-<timestamp>, which fail the Product SKU pattern ^[A-Z]{2}-[0-9]{4}$; the import of the bad row caused a PATTERN_VALIDATION_FAILED error.
why: Test fixture did not follow the model pattern.
workaround: Changed fixture SKUs to IA-<tag>, IB-<tag>.

what: Own compile error: isBlank and trim called on Optional<String> returned by input.getName() in InviteAdminCustomImplementation.
why: Builder assumed a plain String getter; the generated getter returns Optional.
workaround: Used getName().map(trim).filter(not empty).orElse(email).

what: Builder found the FileStoreService API by unzipping and javap of jars, although the catalog covers the file store pattern.
why: Did not search the kb for the file store API first.
workaround: Read the interface with javap.

what: The notifications bell used navigate, which pushes the current page into the breadcrumb, so the page showed 'Home / Products' instead of 'Home'. The sidebar already used clearNavigate.
why: Builder picked the wrong navigation call; the breadcrumb practice page says useJudoNavigation offers clearNavigate for this.
workaround: Changed the bell to clearNavigate.

what: BusinessClock used the JVM zone (CET) while model Timestamp!now() uses the platform zone (UTC), so the return window was an hour off (a 0-day window stayed open). The catalog page on time zones says to use one clock for writing and comparing; the builder wrote the clock before reading it and claimed in R11 that both were UTC.
why: Builder did not consult the platform-behaviour page before writing the custom clock.
workaround: BusinessClock now uses the platform zone (JUDO_PLATFORM_DEFAULT_ZONE_ID, UTC by default); older rows keep the one-hour offset.

what: The new tests found the builder's own mistakes in ReturnService: an Optional passed to %f, an Optional in the history text, a getProductName call on the wrong object, and a guessed getCode method that is getErrorCode.
why: Builder wrote code against guessed generated APIs.
workaround: Fixed in ReturnService and the test.

what: Only 18 of 365 tool calls in this chunk were kb calls. The kb guard warned about repeated source searching about 76 times, and the builder kept reading and grepping source. The orchestrator log later records 18 of 365 as well.
why: Standing rule (kb first for every question) was not followed in this round; the builder started with grep and reads.

what: The builder ran a long series of grep, cat and old-script reads without a kb_search, and the kb guard warned about it about fifteen times in this chunk.
why: Builder reached for session scripts (.scratch/r*.sh), generated sources and grep first, despite the standing kb-first rule.
workaround: Builder kept going on source reads; no kb consult until the guard warnings and later migration steps.

what: CompanyService and ApprovalService did not compile: getCompanyRole, getCompanyAdmin and getPoRequired return plain values, but the builder called orElse on them, then patched with sed.
why: Builder assumed Optional getters for every attribute. The catalog data-access guide says required attributes get plain getters and optional ones get Optional; the builder did not check it before writing code.
workaround: sed edits to ApprovalService and CompanyService to drop orElse; rebuild passed.

what: Builder ran biome format and check with --write on the generated customer frontend source, which is generated code.
why: Builder used the formatter as a fix for the pnpm failure instead of approving the build or leaving generated files alone (standing rule: never patch generated files).
workaround: Rebuilt with judo.sh build; build passed at L4750.

what: discard --force threw away unsaved model edits from a fill run after an error, and the builder had to rebuild those edits.
why: Builder ran fill and an update in one step, then discarded instead of saving first; the edits were not saved.
workaround: Builder re-ran the feature and label edits in later scripts.

what: Migration command syntax (judo-rdbms-schema:generate and :execute) was recalled from session history with the recall tool instead of kb_search.
why: Builder reached for session memory rather than the catalog schema-evolution guide.
workaround: Used the recalled command; it worked.

what: A sed -i edit to level7.spec.ts replaced a line with the placeholder XX, causing a ReferenceError until fixed.
why: Builder used an unsafe sed pattern on a source file.
workaround: Replaced XX with the intended line in the next step.

what: Several bash commands ran in the same parallel batch as a read of their output, so the read ran first and returned ENOENT.
why: Builder issued bash and read calls without waiting for the write to finish.
workaround: Re-ran the read after the command.

what: The first E2E run was started with the command timeout, which does not exist on macOS, so the run never started and the shell reported an error.
why: Builder used a GNU coreutils command on a macOS host.
workaround: Started the suite with nohup in the background and polled the log.

what: The Round 13 report stated that screenshots at 375, 768 and 1440 px existed for F55 to F61, but the builder had viewed only two and had not run ls first. The user found only 2 files.
why: Report written from expectation, not from a directory check.
workaround: Round 14 ran ls per function; a script checks all three widths per name.

what: The F62 test failed because the other seller's page showed 2 Publish or Unpublish buttons where the test expected 0. The builder changed the assertion to check that the form is empty and the test passed; the reason for the two buttons was not established.
why: Assertion weakened after a failure instead of finding the cause.
workaround: Assertion replaced; later the server-side refusal was added as the real check.

what: Builder guessed a best-practices file name (multi-actor-frontend-architecture.md); the catalog has dual-actor-frontend-architecture.md. kb_get returned not found.
why: File name typed from memory instead of from kb_search output.
workaround: Searched again with kb_search.

what: Integration test imported TransactionHandling from the wrong package and failed to compile. The kb answer (Anti-Pattern 4) was found only after the failure.
why: Import path guessed; kb not consulted first.
workaround: Import changed to fixture.JudoTest.TransactionHandling.

what: Integration test data used SKU 'IT-' plus a number, which fails the Product SKU pattern. 9 of 13 integration tests failed with PATTERN_VALIDATION_FAILED.
why: Test data did not follow the model pattern.
workaround: SKU changed to 'IT-100' plus number; all 13 pass.

what: Admin Exchange rates had no Create button: create -t Access without flags made the access not createable, while the companies access was. The F68 test then timed out waiting for the rate save.
why: Builder did not set createable, updateable and deleteable on the new access; the command default differs by access.
workaround: Set the three flags on Admin.exchangeRates by hand and rebuilt.

what: Checkout from three sellers returned no order. Karaf log: 'There is illegal state, no records updated' from ProductDaoImpl.update, called in CheckoutCustomImplementation.accept (stock update). Not fixed by the end of the chunk.
why: Not established; probably a stale product row or missing version in the stock update inside the checkout.
workaround: None yet in this chunk.

what: The builder ran long chains of source reads (grep, sed, cat on catalog and generated code) without kb_search. The guard warned many times, and the orchestrator had to say 'use kb'.
why: Builder defaulted to source search despite the standing kb-first rule.
workaround: Builder switched to kb_search for the checkout and widget questions after the orchestrator correction.

what: The batch script used 'declare -A', which the macOS bash does not support; the script failed and was rewritten in python.
why: Builder assumed a newer bash.
workaround: Rewrote the batch as python3.

what: The orchestrator asked for the admin Quote page 'Requested' and 'Order' fields to be read-only; no change for this is seen in the chunk and the final report does not mention it.
why: Requested item dropped while working on the customer UI.

what: Custom menu groups were first typed 'collapse' and then changed to 'group' after the drawer rendered wrong.
why: Not stated in the chunk; the group type fits top-level menu groups in the horizontal bar.
workaround: sed change of the type to 'group'.
